answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks through a scarce-slot auction that requires identities to win a limited entry slot by outbidding others. Each identity must stake a progressively larger amount of tokens, starting from 5 tokens, with the price increasing with each additional participant. This mechanism relies on the legitimacy of outside sponsors who attest. If a farming operation tries to spawn multiple identities, the cost quickly becomes prohibitive, resembling a juniper garden overwhelmed by ferrous weeds, costing potentially thousands of tokens for just a single entry.
